explanation.en: Examples support points but are not points themselves.

stem.en: "The diplomat's reply was so terse that the journalists hardly had time to raise their pens." Terse means:

explanation.en: The journalists had no time to write: the reply was very short.

stem.en: An inferential question asks you to:

options.en: Work out what the writer suggests but does not state
Copy a sentence from the passage

explanation.en: Inference reads between the lines with evidence.

stem.en: Which sentence is the best one-line summary of the passage?

options.en: Mangroves protect coasts from waves and storms but are being destroyed and are slow to recover.
Prawn farms are profitable in coastal villages.
Rivers carry silt to the sea.

passage.en: Mangroves grow where rivers meet the sea. Their tangled roots trap silt, slowing the waves before they reach the shore. During cyclones, villages behind thick mangroves often suffer far less damage than those without. Yet mangroves are cut for prawn farms and firewood, and once lost they take decades to return.

explanation.en: It includes the main idea (protection), the threat and its seriousness, without details.

stem.en: Choose the correct transformation of "As soon as the teacher entered, the class stood up."

options.en: No sooner had the teacher entered than the class stood up.
No sooner the teacher entered than the class stood up.
No sooner had the teacher entered when the class stood up.
No sooner did the teacher entered than the class stood up.

explanation.en: No sooner + had + subject + past participle … than.

stem.en: Choose the passive of "They will announce the results tomorrow."

options.en: The results will be announced tomorrow.
The results would be announced tomorrow.

explanation.en: Future passive: will be + past participle.

stem.en: He said, "I have finished my homework." In indirect speech:

options.en: He said that he had finished his homework.
He said that he has finished his homework.
He said that I had finished my homework.
He said that he finished his homework now.

explanation.en: Present perfect shifts back to past perfect; I becomes he.

options.en: In spite of being tired, she kept working.
In spite she was tired, she kept working.
Despite of being tired, she kept working.
Despite she was tired, she kept working.

explanation.en: In spite of / Despite + noun or -ing; never "despite of".

solution.en: In spite of / Despite + noun or -ing; never "despite of".

stem.en: Fill in the blank: He has been waiting ___ two hours.
The meeting was ___ because the chairman was ill. (cancelled)

options.en: Neither the teacher nor the students were present.
Neither the teacher nor the students was present.
Neither the teacher or the students were present.
Neither of the teacher nor the students were present.

explanation.en: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject (students → were).
